messages:
incident-bot: pagerduty HIGH: Serving-runtime - gpu-oom spikes during decode/streaming in prod-us-east-1. Node flaps detected. Incident ticket INC-7890. Paging oncall: @sara :rotating_light:

sara: acked. looking now. can someone post recent grafana for p99 decode latency + gpu mem?

david: i'm on call shadow, pulling logs. seeing repeated 'CUDA out of memory' in runner logs during streaming decode for model gpt-large-v2. stack snippet pasted below.

david: ```
2026-02-18T14:02:11Z runner[pid=2321]: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 14.3 GiB already allocated; 512.0 MiB free; 14.35 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  File "/app/serve/decode.py", line 412, in stream_decode
    outputs = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=10000, do_sample=True)
```

david: initial hypothesis: runaway generation because client max_tokens missing / streaming_max_tokens not enforced. a few requests went unbounded and OOM'ed GPUs, causing pods to crash and k8s to restart -> request drops.

sara: confirmed spikes on gpu_mem_usage in grafana at 14:02:10. p99 latency shot to 6s and error rate jumped to 2.1%.

maria: support: got 8 customer error reports in ~5m window. customers reported '503' and broken streams. affected: AcmeCorp (ingest), BetaShop (chat), internal smoke tests.

david: immediate mitigation steps I'm going to try: 1) apply runtime soft cap to streaming endpoints via router (enforce streaming_max_tokens=512) 2) scale up nodepool by +2 g4dn equivalents to reduce crash churn 3) kill pods showing persistent OOM to let autoscaler recreate with clean state

alex: i'll stand by to run the kubectl commands and coordinate scaling.

deploy-bot: starting rollout: routing override config -> /routes/streaming set streaming_max_tokens=512 (user: david)

alex: ran kill on three pods (serve-runtime-xx). kubectl describe shows CrashLoopBackOff with lastExitReason: OOMKilled.

alex: scaled nodepool "inference-us-east-1" +2 instances via cloud autoscaler. new nodes coming up.

david: routing override accepted by control plane. forcing fallback for model gpt-large-v2 -> gpt-medium-v2 for new requests when predicted token count > 512. snippet:

```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate/stream",
  "overrides": {
    "streaming_max_tokens": 512,
    "fallback_model": "gpt-medium-v2"
  }
}
```

sara: paused streaming feature flag for prod (feature-ff/streaming) to prevent more runaways. note: this will affect some customers relying on streaming, communicating to support.

maria: sending customer comms now: brief outage notice + ETA-estimate. logging contact with AcmeCorp success team.

david: after routing override + pod restarts, memory pressure dropped and OOM errors stopped. monitoring for 10m to confirm stability.

support-bot: AcmeCorp reported partial recovery; BetaShop still saw one failed request at 14:07. total errors recorded by LB: ~1,210 dropped requests between 14:01:20 - 14:06:40.

alex: good. opening a temporary acceptance rule to hard-fail requests with client max_tokens > 2048 at the edge (nginx/gateway) to prevent runaway token requests.

david: note for root cause: model generate call didn't have a server-side enforced max_new_tokens limit in the runtime for streaming API path. patch proposed: enforce global streaming_max_tokens default = 1024 (config override lower priority than per-route) and add accounting in decoder loop to preemptively stop and return trimmed response when limit reached.

sara: handing off to david for post-incident follow up. i'll write short incident-notes and coordinate timeline. i'm now off pager for the next 2h.

david: taking over. immediate followups: 1) postmortem doc (owners: david+alex) 2) backfill runbook step to include 'enforce streaming_max_tokens at control plane' 3) prioritize hotfix to runtime to check for max_new_tokens on model.generate path 4) add integration test that simulates runaway generation and ensures circuit breaker trips

maria: support will compile customer impact table and send to PMs + legal if needed. initial affected customers: AcmeCorp, BetaShop, internal QA.

david: timeline note: incident start ~1746500120 (first OOM log), mitigation applied 1746500405 (routing override + kill), stable at 1746500720, verified recovery at 1746501600. approximate dropped requests 1210.

alex: I'll file CL to nginx edge to hard-fail >2048 tokens in next cohort.

david: paste of quick hotfix patch we applied to router for auditors:

```diff
--- a/router/config.py
+++ b/router/config.py
@@ -87,6 +87,12 @@
         if route.get('streaming'):
-            route['streaming_max_tokens'] = route.get('streaming_max_tokens', None)
+            # enforce a safe default to prevent unbounded streaming gen
+            route['streaming_max_tokens'] = min(route.get('streaming_max_tokens', 1024), 2048)
+            if route['streaming_max_tokens'] <= 0:
+                route['streaming_max_tokens'] = 512
+            # log enforcement for incident tracing
+            audit.log('streaming_cap_enforced', route_id=route['id'], value=route['streaming_max_tokens'])
```

sara: thanks team. I'm adding "customer impact" and "next steps" to INC-7890. please add any missing notes to the ticket.

maria: posted customer email draft to INC-7890, tagging PMs.

david: follow-ups (owners): 
- david: runtime hotfix to check model.generate max_new_tokens + add decoder accounting (PR queued)
- alex: nginx edge hard-fail rule + infra test (PR queued)
- sara: update oncall runbook and escalate docs (in progress)
- maria: final customer impact report + outreach (in progress)

incident-bot: incident INC-7890 marked mitigated by david at 1746501600. severity: high -> downgraded to medium; timeline and notes attached to ticket.

alex: anyone want to do a quick blameless sync in 30m to capture any missing operational gaps?

david: yes, let's do 30m. invite: #eng-runtime postmortem.

sara: offcall. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
